metadata.name: Deque-style Web Accessibility Checklist Map
metadata.basis: Paraphrased mapping of Deque University Web Accessibility Checklist topics and WCAG A/AA requirements for AI-assisted review.

items.topic: Structure and Semantics / Page Title
items.requirement: The page has a present, meaningful, accurate title that updates when the page purpose or state changes.
manualSteps: Open the captured page or scenario state.
Read the browser tab title and compare it with the page purpose.
If this is a single-page app, perform the state-changing action again and confirm the title changes when the purpose changes.
Confirm the title is concise and distinguishes this page from other pages in the same journey.
items.passCriteria: Title exists, is accurate for the page/state, and changes when navigation or scripted context change creates a new page purpose.
items.naCriteria: N/A only for non-HTML content where a page title concept does not apply.

items.topic: Structure and Semantics / Language
items.requirement: The page language and any meaningful language changes are programmatically identified with valid language codes.
manualSteps: Confirm the main page language matches the `lang` value on the html element.
Find any visible text in a different human language.
Inspect those language changes and confirm they have a valid `lang` attribute on or above the changed text.
Use a screen reader spot check if pronunciation is important.
items.passCriteria: Primary language is set accurately and meaningful inline language changes are marked.
items.naCriteria: Language-of-parts is N/A when all meaningful content is in the same language.

items.topic: Structure and Semantics / Headings
items.requirement: Headings are real headings, meaningful, and form a useful page outline without using heading markup for non-headings.
manualSteps: Review the heading list from the evidence report.
Visually scan the page and identify text that appears to start sections.
Confirm visible section headings are represented as headings in the evidence.
Confirm heading text accurately describes the content that follows.
Confirm heading levels make sense for the page structure.
items.passCriteria: Headings are semantic, meaningful, and useful for navigation; decorative or styling-only text is not marked as a heading.
items.naCriteria: N/A only for a page state with no sectioned content where headings would not help navigation.

items.topic: Structure and Semantics / Landmarks
items.requirement: Landmarks identify major page regions, support bypassing repeated content, and duplicate landmark types are distinguishable where needed.
manualSteps: Review the landmark list.
Confirm the page has an identifiable main content region.
Confirm navigation, search, banner, complementary, and contentinfo regions are present when visually applicable.
If multiple landmarks of the same role exist, confirm their accessible names distinguish them.
Use a screen reader landmark shortcut to confirm the regions are announced usefully.
items.passCriteria: Major regions are discoverable and repeated blocks can be bypassed using landmarks, headings, or skip links.
items.naCriteria: N/A only for a very small embedded page fragment where landmarks are not part of the delivered UI.

items.topic: Structure and Semantics / Lists
items.requirement: Content that is a list is represented with appropriate list semantics.
manualSteps: Visually identify grouped items that function as ordered, unordered, or description lists.
Compare them with the list inventory.
Confirm list item counts and nesting are meaningful to screen reader users.
Confirm non-list content is not forced into list semantics.
items.passCriteria: Real lists use list semantics and list structure matches visual grouping.
items.naCriteria: N/A when the page state has no list-like content.

items.topic: Structure and Semantics / Tables
items.requirement: Data tables expose headers, associations, and names/captions as needed; layout tables do not expose misleading headers.
manualSteps: Identify every data table in the page state.
Confirm column and row headers are marked as headers.
For complex tables, confirm each data cell is associated with the correct headers.
Confirm table captions or names describe the purpose when needed.
Confirm purely layout tables do not contain data-table headers.
items.passCriteria: Screen reader users can determine the same table relationships visible users can determine.
items.naCriteria: N/A when no data or layout tables exist in the page state.

items.topic: Structure and Semantics / Iframes
items.requirement: Frames and iframes have accurate titles, and embedded documents have meaningful titles when user-facing.
manualSteps: Review each iframe or frame in the evidence.
Confirm the parent-page frame title describes the embedded content or purpose.
Open or inspect user-facing embedded content and confirm its document title is meaningful.
Confirm hidden/empty frames are hidden from assistive technologies when they convey no user content.
items.passCriteria: Each user-facing frame is named accurately and hidden frames do not create noise.
items.naCriteria: N/A when the page state has no iframe or frame elements.

items.topic: Structure and Semantics / Markup Validity
items.requirement: For WCAG 2.2, the former Parsing success criterion is obsolete; still review severe invalid markup when it breaks names, roles, states, focus, labels, or relationships.
manualSteps: Confirm the requested WCAG version.
For WCAG 2.2, do not fail the page solely for generic HTML parsing issues.
Review invalid or unusual markup only when it causes an accessibility failure, such as broken labels, duplicate IDs affecting ARIA references, invalid roles, missing names, or incorrect states.
If testing WCAG 2.0 or 2.1 in an organizational policy, document how the project treats the obsolete Parsing criterion.
items.passCriteria: No markup issue creates an accessibility failure in names, roles, values, relationships, or operation.
items.naCriteria: N/A only when the audit scope explicitly excludes markup validity and no related accessibility behavior is affected.

items.topic: Structure and Semantics / Other Semantic Elements
items.requirement: Semantic elements such as emphasis, highlights, quotes, inserted text, and deleted text communicate meaning without relying only on visual styling.
manualSteps: Find text where emphasis, highlighting, quotations, inserted text, or deleted text changes meaning.
Confirm the meaning is available in text or semantic markup, not only color, bold, italics, indentation, or strikethrough styling.
Use a screen reader spot check for any critical semantic text.
items.passCriteria: Meaning conveyed by text styling is also conveyed semantically or textually.
items.naCriteria: N/A when no emphasized, highlighted, quoted, inserted, or deleted text carries meaning.

items.topic: Links and Navigation / Links
items.requirement: Links use appropriate link semantics, have discernible names, and their purpose is understandable from text or immediate context.
manualSteps: Review all links with empty, duplicate, vague, or suspicious names.
Confirm each link purpose is understandable from its name or immediate context.
Confirm links are used for navigation and buttons are used for in-page actions where practical.
Confirm file, external-site, or new-window behavior is announced or visually indicated when needed.
items.passCriteria: Each link has a meaningful accessible name and users can predict its destination or purpose.
items.naCriteria: N/A when there are no links in the page state.

items.topic: Links and Navigation / Link Keyboard Access
items.requirement: Links are keyboard focusable, activate with Enter, appear in logical order, and show visible focus.
manualSteps: Use Tab and Shift+Tab to reach every visible link.
Confirm focus order follows the visual and task order.
Confirm the focus indicator is visible on each link.
Press Enter on representative links and confirm activation works.
Confirm positive tabindex is not creating a custom tab order.
items.passCriteria: Links are reachable, visible when focused, logically ordered, and keyboard-operable.
items.naCriteria: N/A when the page state has no links.

items.topic: Links and Navigation / Link Visual Design
items.requirement: Links are visually distinguishable from surrounding text, meet contrast expectations, and provide hover/focus indications.
manualSteps: Inspect links embedded in body text.
Confirm color is not the only visual cue unless contrast and focus/hover cues satisfy the requirement.
Check representative links with hover and keyboard focus.
Review automated contrast findings for text and focus indicators.
items.passCriteria: Sighted users can identify links and perceive focus/hover state without relying on color alone.
items.naCriteria: N/A when there are no visible links or all links are controls/buttons with clear visual affordance.

items.topic: Links and Navigation / Site Navigation
items.requirement: Repeated navigation, repeated help, and repeated functionality are consistently ordered and identified; users have multiple ways to locate pages when applicable.
manualSteps: Compare this page with at least one other page from the same flow or site section.
Confirm repeated navigation appears in the same relative order.
Confirm repeated controls or labels with the same function use consistent names.
Confirm repeated help mechanisms appear in a consistent relative order.
For sites with multiple pages, confirm at least two ways exist to find pages, such as navigation, search, sitemap, table of contents, or related links.
items.passCriteria: Repeated navigation/help/functionality stays consistent and users can find pages in more than one way when required.
items.naCriteria: N/A for a single-page isolated app or embedded widget with no repeated navigation or multipage site context.

items.topic: Links and Navigation / Within-Page Navigation
items.requirement: Users can bypass repeated blocks and navigate within the page using skip links, headings, landmarks, table of contents, or equivalent methods.
manualSteps: Press Tab from the top of the page and check whether a skip link appears when appropriate.
Activate the skip link and confirm focus moves to the intended target.
Use headings and landmarks to bypass repeated content with a screen reader.
If a table of contents or pagination exists, confirm current position is visible and programmatically available.
If single-key shortcuts exist, confirm they can be disabled, remapped, or limited to focused components.
items.passCriteria: Repeated content can be bypassed and within-page navigation is logical and discoverable.
items.naCriteria: N/A only when there are no repeated blocks or long sections where bypass methods would be useful.

items.topic: Links and Navigation / Reading and Focus Order
items.requirement: Reading order and keyboard focus order are logical, intuitive, and do not rely on positive tabindex.
manualSteps: Read through the visible page from top to bottom and left to right according to the language/layout.
Compare the visual order with the DOM and accessibility order evidence.
Press Tab through every focusable element and confirm focus follows a logical task order.
Press Shift+Tab through part of the page and confirm reverse order is logical.
Confirm no visible interactive control is skipped and no hidden control receives unexpected focus.
Review any positive tabindex values and confirm they are removed or justified.
items.passCriteria: Reading and focus order match the intended content/task sequence and remain understandable for keyboard and screen reader users.
items.naCriteria: N/A is rarely valid; only for static non-interactive fragments where reading order is trivially linear.

items.topic: Images and Visual Design / Images
items.requirement: Informative, active, complex, background, SVG, canvas, and icon images expose appropriate alternatives; decorative images are ignored.
manualSteps: Review every image or image-like element from the evidence.
For informative images, confirm alternative text conveys purpose and author intent.
For linked or button images, confirm the name describes the destination or action.
For complex images, confirm a short alternative plus an extended description exists.
For decorative images, confirm they are hidden or have empty alternatives.
For informative background images, confirm equivalent visible or programmatic text exists.
items.passCriteria: Image alternatives match each image's purpose and decorative images do not add noise.
items.naCriteria: N/A when the page state contains no images, SVGs, canvas, icon fonts, or informative CSS background images.

items.topic: Images and Visual Design / Images of Text
items.requirement: Informative text is not presented as an image when real text can provide the same visual result; image text still meets contrast when used.
manualSteps: Inspect images and background images for text content.
Confirm text-in-image is essential, such as a logo, or customizable if needed.
Confirm equivalent real text is provided when the image text conveys information.
Check contrast for any necessary image text.
items.passCriteria: Informative text is real text unless an exception applies, and necessary image text is perceivable.
items.naCriteria: N/A when no images or backgrounds contain informative text.

items.topic: Images and Visual Design / Color and Contrast
items.requirement: Text, images of text, UI component boundaries, graphical objects, and focus indicators meet required contrast; color is not the only way meaning is conveyed.
manualSteps: Review automated contrast violations.
Inspect information conveyed by color, such as status, charts, errors, or required fields.
Confirm each color-coded meaning has text, icon shape, pattern, or programmatic alternative.
Inspect UI boundaries and focus indicators against adjacent colors.
Use a contrast analyzer for samples axe cannot measure, such as gradients, images, disabled states, and canvas.
items.passCriteria: Required contrast ratios are met and meaning is not communicated by color alone.
items.naCriteria: N/A only for subchecks that have no corresponding content, such as no UI component boundaries or no color-coded information.

items.topic: Images and Visual Design / Text Styles, Resize, Reflow, and Zoom
items.requirement: Content remains usable at text resize/zoom and small viewport widths, without two-direction scrolling unless essential.
manualSteps: Set browser zoom or text zoom to 200 percent and inspect the page.
At 320 CSS pixels wide for vertical content, confirm only one scroll direction is needed unless two directions are essential.
Apply text spacing settings: line height 1.5, paragraph spacing 2, letter spacing 0.12em, word spacing 0.16em.
Confirm no content or functionality is lost, clipped, overlapped, or hidden.
On mobile, confirm pinch zoom is not disabled.
items.passCriteria: Users can read and operate the page with zoom, text spacing, and narrow viewport conditions.
items.naCriteria: N/A only for specific subchecks where the content type is absent, such as no text content for text spacing.

items.topic: Images and Visual Design / Visual Cues
items.requirement: Meaning is not conveyed only through visual characteristics such as shape, size, location, orientation, or proximity.
manualSteps: Look for instructions such as 'click the green button', 'fields on the right', or 'items marked with a star'.
Confirm the same meaning is available in text or programmatically.
Check labels are visually close to related controls.
Confirm layout and visual emphasis do not create ambiguity about the primary task.
items.passCriteria: Users can understand instructions and relationships without relying only on sensory or visual cues.
items.naCriteria: N/A when no instructions or relationships depend on visual characteristics.

items.topic: Images and Visual Design / Adaptive and Responsive Output
items.requirement: Content works in portrait and landscape, adapts to small viewports, and preserves essential information when simplified.
manualSteps: Test the page in portrait and landscape orientations or equivalent viewport sizes.
Confirm the UI does not force one orientation unless essential.
Review the narrow viewport screenshot and live page for clipping, overlap, or hidden controls.
Confirm simplification on small screens does not remove essential content or functionality.
items.passCriteria: Page content and controls adapt without losing meaning or operation.
items.naCriteria: N/A only when orientation or responsive behavior is not applicable to the delivery context.

items.topic: Multimedia, Animations, and Motion / Audio and Video
items.requirement: Audio/video media have required transcripts, captions, audio descriptions, audio controls, autoplay controls, and accessible media-player controls.
manualSteps: Identify all prerecorded and live audio/video content in the page state.
For audio-only, confirm a transcript exists.
For prerecorded video/multimedia, confirm captions and audio description are available where required.
For live multimedia, confirm synchronized captions are available.
If media autoplays, confirm users can pause, stop, hide, mute, or control volume as required.
Operate media-player controls with keyboard and screen reader.
items.passCriteria: Media alternatives and controls make the content usable for deaf, hard-of-hearing, blind, low-vision, keyboard, and screen reader users.
items.naCriteria: N/A when no audio, video, video-like animation, media player, or background media exists in the page state.

items.topic: Multimedia, Animations, and Motion / Animation, Motion, and Timed Content
items.requirement: Flashing, parallax, animation, autoplay, and time limits are controlled and do not block keyboard or assistive technology use.
manualSteps: Observe the page for flashing, auto-updating, parallax, moving backgrounds, animation, or timed sessions.
Confirm content does not flash more than allowed thresholds.
Confirm moving/parallax content and controls are keyboard accessible.
Confirm text and UI contrast remains sufficient over moving backgrounds.
Confirm users can pause, stop, hide, extend, or adjust timed content when required.
Confirm timed content can be replayed when replay is needed and does not alter meaning.
items.passCriteria: Motion and timing do not create seizure risk, loss of access, or unexpected time pressure.
items.naCriteria: N/A when no flashing, animation, motion, autoplaying content, or time limits exist.

items.topic: User Input, Forms, and Dynamic Content / Device-Independent User Input
items.requirement: All functionality is available from keyboard, focus is visible, focus is not trapped, shortcuts do not conflict, and custom keystrokes have instructions.
manualSteps: Use only the keyboard to reach and operate every visible control.
Confirm Tab and Shift+Tab movement is logical.
Confirm every focused element has a visible focus indicator and is not fully obscured.
Confirm Enter, Space, Escape, and arrow keys work according to control type.
Confirm keyboard focus can enter and leave widgets unless a modal focus trap is intentionally active.
Confirm page-defined single-key shortcuts can be disabled, remapped, or are active only in focused controls.
Confirm custom keyboard interactions have visible and programmatic instructions.
items.passCriteria: All page functionality is operable by keyboard without trap, loss of focus, missing focus indicator, or unexplained custom keys.
items.naCriteria: N/A only for non-interactive static content; individual shortcut subchecks are N/A when no shortcuts exist.

items.topic: User Input, Forms, and Dynamic Content / Focus Management During Interactions
items.requirement: When actions change context, focus moves intentionally to useful text and is not lost or reset unexpectedly.
manualSteps: Trigger each interaction that opens a dialog, menu, panel, route, error summary, toast, or dynamic result.
Observe where keyboard focus moves.
Confirm focus moves to the most useful next element when context changes.
Confirm focus never disappears, returns to the top unexpectedly, or lands on an unnamed element.
Close transient UI and confirm focus returns to a logical invoking element.
items.passCriteria: Focus movement supports the user's task and screen reader users receive the context change.
items.naCriteria: N/A when the page state has no interactions that change context or content.

items.topic: User Input, Forms, and Dynamic Content / Pointer, Touch, and Voice
items.requirement: Pointer and touch functionality has accessible target size, cancellation, alternatives for drag/path gestures, and label-in-name support for voice control.
manualSteps: Review target-size candidates under 24 by 24 CSS pixels.
Confirm small targets meet an allowed exception or have an equivalent larger target.
Test pointer interactions and confirm activation is not only on down-event unless essential.
For drag, swipe, multipoint, or path gestures, confirm a single-pointer non-gesture alternative exists unless essential.
For motion-actuated features, confirm UI alternatives exist and motion activation can be disabled.
Use voice-control reasoning: confirm visible label text is included in the programmatic name.
items.passCriteria: Users can operate controls with pointer, touch, and voice without precision-only, gesture-only, or mismatched-label barriers.
items.naCriteria: N/A for subchecks where no pointer-specific custom target, drag gesture, touch gesture, voice-labeled control, or motion actuation exists.

items.topic: User Input, Forms, and Dynamic Content / Form Inputs, Labels, and Instructions
items.requirement: Inputs and input groups have visible, meaningful, programmatic labels that do not rely only on placeholder text or sensory references.
manualSteps: Review each input, select, textarea, checkbox, radio, switch, slider, and combobox.
Confirm each has a visible label unless a self-evident icon is used with a programmatic name.
Confirm each label is programmatically associated and available as text.
Confirm placeholder text is not the only label.
Confirm visible label text is included in the accessible name.
For grouped inputs, confirm group labels are visible, meaningful, and programmatically associated.
items.passCriteria: Every form control and group can be understood visually, by screen reader, and by voice-control users.
items.naCriteria: N/A when no form inputs or form-like custom controls exist.

items.topic: User Input, Forms, and Dynamic Content / Input Purpose and Instructions
items.requirement: Common personal-data input purposes, field instructions, restrictions, required state, and disabled-field meaning are communicated visibly and programmatically.
manualSteps: For personal-data fields, confirm appropriate autocomplete/input purpose is used where applicable.
Confirm input instructions and format restrictions are visible, meaningful, and programmatically associated.
Confirm required fields are indicated visually and, where possible, programmatically.
Confirm disabled fields that are essential to understanding are explained outside the disabled control.
Confirm instructions do not rely only on shape, color, position, or other sensory cues.
items.passCriteria: Users know what to enter, which fields are required, and any restrictions before or during input.
items.naCriteria: N/A when no fields collect data or require instructions/restrictions; autocomplete is N/A when no covered personal-data fields exist.

items.topic: User Input, Forms, and Dynamic Content / Time Limits, Redundant Entry, and Authentication
items.requirement: Forms provide sufficient time, avoid unnecessary repeated entry, and do not require unsupported cognitive-function tests for authentication.
manualSteps: Confirm whether the form or session has a time limit.
If timed, confirm users can turn off, adjust, extend, or otherwise receive sufficient time unless timing is essential.
Walk through the process and identify information the user must enter more than once.
Confirm repeated information is auto-populated or selectable unless an allowed exception applies.
For authentication, confirm users can use password managers, paste, or alternative methods and are not forced to solve an unsupported cognitive test.
items.passCriteria: Time pressure, repeated entry, and authentication do not create avoidable barriers.
items.naCriteria: N/A when there is no form process, no time limit, no repeated-entry process, or no authentication step, respectively.

items.topic: User Input, Forms, and Dynamic Content / Form Validation and Feedback
items.requirement: Errors are identified, described, suggested, visible, and programmatically associated; critical submissions provide prevention or confirmation.
manualSteps: Submit invalid or incomplete data for each form state.
Confirm the page identifies each field in error and describes the error in text.
Confirm error text is visible and programmatically associated with the field or summary.
Confirm known suggestions are provided unless they would harm security or purpose.
Confirm focus moves to a useful error summary or remains in a logical place.
For legal, financial, user-data, or test submissions, confirm reversible, checked, or confirmed submission is available.
Confirm success messages are perceivable when submission succeeds.
items.passCriteria: Users can find, understand, and correct errors and avoid serious accidental submissions.
items.naCriteria: N/A when no forms or user-submitted input exist; critical error prevention is N/A when submissions are not legal, financial, user-data, or test responses.

items.topic: User Input, Forms, and Dynamic Content / Dynamic Content
items.requirement: Dynamic changes do not surprise users, and important added content is communicated visually and to assistive technologies.
manualSteps: Trigger every dynamic update: expand/collapse, filter, sort, load more, route change, modal, toast, validation, or search result.
Confirm changing focus alone does not trigger unexpected context changes.
Confirm input or selection changes do not unexpectedly navigate, open windows, or move focus unless users were informed first.
Confirm important added content is announced or focus is moved appropriately.
If a session timeout exists, confirm users are warned and can save or extend time.
items.passCriteria: Dynamic updates are predictable and perceivable to keyboard and screen reader users.
items.naCriteria: N/A when no JavaScript-driven content changes, popups, live updates, or timeouts exist.

items.topic: User Input, Forms, and Dynamic Content / Custom Widgets
items.requirement: Custom widgets expose correct name, role, value, state, and changes to assistive technologies.
manualSteps: Identify custom controls and ARIA widgets from the evidence.
Confirm each interactive widget has an accessible name.
Confirm each widget exposes the correct native element or ARIA role.
Confirm value and initial state are exposed programmatically.
Interact with the widget and confirm state changes are reflected visually and to assistive technologies.
Confirm non-ARIA state changes are communicated with live regions, focus movement, or equivalent methods.
items.passCriteria: Screen reader users can identify and operate the widget with accurate name, role, value, and state updates.
items.naCriteria: N/A when no custom widgets or ARIA-enhanced controls exist.

items.topic: User Input, Forms, and Dynamic Content / Custom Widget Keyboard Patterns
items.requirement: Custom widgets follow expected keyboard conventions and provide instructions for non-standard interaction models.
manualSteps: Identify widget type, such as accordion, dialog, combobox, menu, tabs, slider, tree, grid, tooltip, toolbar, or carousel.
Compare keyboard behavior with the corresponding WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices pattern.
Confirm Tab moves into/out of the widget correctly and arrow keys work where expected.
Confirm Escape, Enter, and Space behavior is appropriate for the widget type.
Confirm instructions are provided when interaction is not obvious.
items.passCriteria: Custom widget keyboard behavior matches user expectations and does not trap or confuse users.
items.naCriteria: N/A when no custom widget patterns exist and native controls provide built-in behavior.

items.topic: User Input, Forms, and Dynamic Content / CAPTCHA
items.requirement: CAPTCHA is avoided where possible; when present it has purpose text, alternatives across sensory modalities, keyboard access, dynamic-content support, widget accessibility, and contrast.
manualSteps: Confirm whether a CAPTCHA or human verification challenge is present.
If present, confirm non-text CAPTCHA has text that explains its purpose.
Confirm an alternative sensory modality is available when needed.
Confirm at least one text-based option exists or an accessible alternative process is available for deafblind users.
Operate CAPTCHA controls with keyboard only.
Apply dynamic content, custom widget, and color contrast checks to CAPTCHA UI.
items.passCriteria: The challenge does not block users with sensory, cognitive, keyboard, or assistive technology needs.
items.naCriteria: N/A when no CAPTCHA or human verification challenge is present in the page state.
